title: Memanusack (Stony Brook)
summary: Memanusack, also recorded as Memanusuck, is connected with the stream from which Stony Brook takes its name. The waterway is described as an outlet from a pond into the harbor.
translation_content:
The name is interpreted as a place where two streams meet or a brook connecting two ponds, from language connected with gathering together and with a brook or outlet.

Why Place Names Matter

“Place names are important. They can tell us more than the name of a specific spot on the map. They are used to guide us through the world by labeling specific markers for travelers. But place names signify the spiritual or cultural importance of a place, and often indicate the presence of a people.”

— John Flynn, Native Places: An Indigenous Atlas of Utah and the Intermountain West (2020), opening paragraph
whereintheworld_content: Map location note: The pin is placed near the Stony Brook stream and harbor outlet area to represent the waterway association. It is offset slightly from nearby Cutsgunsuck for map visibility and is not an exact surveyed stream point.
